title: How a nuclear bunker is built

lines.text: This is how you build a bunker that can survive a nuclear war.
First, you dig. Every layer of dirt cuts incoming radiation in half.
Stack ten of those halvings, and only about one thousandth gets through.
Next comes a cage of steel rebar.
Then concrete is poured around it. Commercial bunkers often use walls about fifty centimeters thick.
The entrance gets a blast door, set deep into its frame so a shock wave can't pry the edge open.
And there's always a second way out. An emergency escape hatch.
Air is the hard part. Outside air is pulled through a pre filter, a HEPA filter, and activated carbon.
The shelter keeps its air pressure higher than outside, so dust gets pushed out, not sucked in.
Inside, you need bunks, water, food, power, and a radio.
Finally, the whole thing is buried under tons of earth.
Then you wait. Fallout loses most of its strength over the first few weeks.
Would you last a month down here?
